content.title: About
content.content: Chili with chicken is a spicy dish where bite‑size pieces of chicken breast are simmered in a sauce made from tomatoes, beans, chili peppers, and aromatic spices. The dish is popular in American, Mexican, and South American cuisines, offering protein, fiber, and moderate fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally chili is cooked in large pots, allowing flavors to meld over time.
There are many variations: beef, turkey, bean‑only, and vegetarian versions.
Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which provides heat and may boost metabolism.
The dish is often served with rice, corn tortillas, or guacamole.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The recipe supplies vitamins B6 and B12, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Beans and vegetables add dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Tomatoes and chili peppers are rich in lycopene and vitamin C, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: When prepared with minimal added oil, chili with chicken remains low in saturated fats.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Capsaicin can cause stomach irritation in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made broths or sauces can raise salt levels; adjust seasoning accordingly.

items.title: Beans and gas
items.content: Legumes may cause bloating for some; soaking beans before cooking can reduce this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot chili with chicken over steamed rice, with corn tortillas, a dollop of sour cream, or shredded cheese. Fresh cilantro, lime wedges, or guacamole add brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
